title: Statistical levels and spatial modes of Fock-space heterogeneity in many-body localization crossovers
abstract: Near many-body localization crossovers, local memory fluctuates strongly among eigenstates and ensemble realizations, but the observed heterogeneity   combines contributions from different statistical levels. We develop a statistical framework based on configuration-space distance distributions that uses   a variance decomposition to separate fluctuations within eigenstates, between eigenstates of one sample, and between samples. Applying this framework to   random-cosine and quasiperiodic-cosine Ising ensembles with the same one-site field marginal, we find that, at the exact-diagonalization sizes studied,   the clearest difference occurs among disorder realizations or quasiperiodic phase samples, whereas within-eigenstate and within-sample eigenstate-to-   eigenstate contributions remain broadly comparable. Spatial covariances show that random outer fluctuations have a much stronger uniform component,   whereas quasiperiodic phase fluctuations are organized more strongly at finite wave number and partly cancel in the spatial average controlling the   distance center. We find that, near the crossover in the random ensemble, the ensemble-averaged distance center is particularly sensitive to changes in   the nominal field strength. Combined with sample-to-sample differences in the realized field amplitude, this mean response accounts for much of the   sample-to-sample variation in the distance center. Analysis of half-chain entanglement further shows that its sample-to-sample fluctuations likewise   reflect the combined effects of amplitude variations and its own mean response. An application to a fixed-magnetization spin chain demonstrates the   framework in a constrained configuration space. Resolving both statistical level and spatial mode therefore provides a more complete picture of sample-   dependent many-body memory and its configuration-space probability geometry.
summary: This work introduces a statistical framework using configuration-space distance distributions to dissect the sources of sample-to-sample fluctuations in many-body systems near MBL crossovers. By decomposing the total variance into contributions from within eigenstates, between states, and between samples, the authors pinpoint that sample variation is dominated by outer-ensemble effects. This provides a detailed geometric picture of sample-dependent quantum memory.
main_problem: The paper aims to understand the origins and size dependence of sample-to-sample fluctuations in many-body systems, particularly near many-body localization (MBL) crossovers.
main_result: The clearest source of heterogeneity is found at the sample-to-sample level, and the analysis successfully separates contributions from within eigenstates, between eigenstates, and across different physical samples.
method: The authors develop a statistical framework based on configuration-space distance distributions and employ variance decomposition to hierarchically separate fluctuation sources.
model_or_system: The study applies this framework to random-cosine and quasiperiodic-cosine Ising ensembles, comparing them to a fixed-magnetization spin chain.
key_observables: Configuration-space distance distribution, distance center, and the decomposition of total variance into intra-eigenstate, state-to-state, and outer-ensemble contributions.
important_parameters: Nominal field strength, system size (at exact diagonalization limits), and the type of disorder (random vs. quasiperiodic).
main_assumptions: The primary findings are based on calculations performed at exact diagonalization sizes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the variance hierarchy and entropy channels, comparing random and quasiperiodic ensembles across different system sizes and field strengths.
paper_structure: The paper develops a statistical framework using distance distributions and variance decomposition, applies it to random and quasiperiodic Ising models, and analyzes the spatial organization of fluctuations across different statistical levels.
why_interesting: The rigorous statistical decomposition of memory fluctuations across different ensemble realizations provides a powerful diagnostic tool for understanding sample-dependent physics in disordered quantum systems, which is highly relevant to AMO and open quantum systems.

(a) Two configurations drawn independently according to the configuration probability distribution pψ(s) of one eigenstate define Pψ(R). (b) A smaller mean squared local polarization gives a larger mean distance, while the variance contains local and two-point z-spin structure. (c) The mixtures Pan →¯Pa →¯P separate intra-eigenstate variance, state-to-state center variance, and outer-center variance. The colors identify samples a, with several eigenstates shown for each sample. A sample is a disorder realization or is defined by one quasiperiodic phase offset. All curves, displacements, and markers are schematic.

FIG. 2. Illustration of the nested distance hierarchy in the uniform-random open Ising chain at L = 15 and NE = 50. The columns use W = 0.5, 3.259, and 8, spanning thermal-like, crossover, and localized-like profiles. The rows show selected normalized intra-eigenstate distributions Pan(R), selected state-averaged distributions ¯Pa(R), and the full mixture ¯P(R). The shaded band in the bottom row is the pointwise 10th–90th percentile envelope of ¯Pa(R) among outer realizations. Individual curves illustrate the conditioning levels.

FIG. 4. Matched-cosine fluctuation channels re-expressed through the descriptive local-memory coordinate µ/L. Pan- els (a) and (b) show χstate/L for RC and QP, and panels (c) and (d) show χouter/L, for L = 8, . . . , 15 and NE = 100. RC samples are disorder realizations and QP samples are defined by global quasiperiodic phase offsets. The channels use the population normalization of Eq. (6). Each curve follows its own native-W route; equal µ/L denotes equal basis-resolved average local memory.

FIG. 3. Variance anatomy along the native finite-size crossover routes of the open Ising chain with the matched RC (left) and QP (right) fields. From top to bottom, the rows show Vartotal(RH)/L, χintra/L, χstate/L, and χouter/L for L = 8, . . . , 15 and NE = 100. Outer samples are indepen- dent RC phase patterns or QP global phases. All channels use the population normalization of Sec. II B and satisfy Eq. (7). The horizontal axis is each ensemble’s native amplitude W.
